FACT_ID: sec08-F01 | anchor: A01
Defensive driving rests on eight habits: prepare and look ahead, hold correct speed, signal turns and lane changes, allow space, wear the belt, shun weary medicated or drinking driving, keep the vehicle sound, and pocket handheld devices. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=45]

FACT_ID: sec08-F02 | anchor: A01
Drivers sit upright gripping with both hands since slouching or single-hand control turns dangerous, scan far ahead past the nearest road and lead car, sweep eyes and mirrors every few seconds, and assume side-road drivers will blow through stop and yield signs. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=45]

FACT_ID: sec08-F03 | anchor: A01
Distraction means anything stealing driving attention, crashes through injury death or damage, and strikes through mental drift as surely as eyes or hands off task, so drivers banish phones texts arguments eating, restrain children, kennel pets, and answer for safe operation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=45]

FACT_ID: sec08-F04 | anchor: A02
Aggression covers speeding into tailgating, unsignaled darting lane changes, shoulder and unpaved passing, bullying slower users, running signs signals and stopped school buses, straying left, impaired reckless running, and crosses into road rage upon trying to hurt another driver. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=46]

FACT_ID: sec08-F05 | anchor: A02
The confronted driver skips eye contact, stays calm, slips away safely, never races or guards lane turf, belts all aboard, ignores taunts, phones in description location plates and direction, flees followers to a police station without stopping, and waits clear of caused crashes to brief police. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=46]

FACT_ID: sec08-F06 | anchor: A02
Drivers dodge their own aggression with generous travel time, off-peak scheduling, late-call relief, calm rested sober starts, soothing cabins, loose posture, courteous forgiveness, refusal to retaliate, and yielded rights-of-way since brief waits beat twisted metal. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=46]

FACT_ID: sec08-F07 | anchor: A02
Road rage means angry hostile operation boiling into violent criminal acts including provocation and intimidation, differs from aggression as criminal versus traffic violation, can seize anyone, and draws fines jail probation plus suspension or revocation. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=46]

FACT_ID: sec08-F08 | anchor: A03
Rage acts span shouted horn obscene threats, cutoffs tailgates blocks chases run-offs and rammings, and roadside exits to menace assault or injure, while rage degrades blood pressure reason and judgment, multiplies mistakes and crashes, and forfeits licenses families jobs and clean records. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=47]

FACT_ID: sec08-F09 | anchor: A03
State law forces every approved crash course to teach rage hazards via motor-vehicle offices and sites, while speed law caps unposted roads at fifty-five, preaches sub-limit sense on slick fogged expressways where fifty still earns unreasonable tickets, honors minimums, and holds New York City to twenty-five unless posted. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=47]

FACT_ID: sec08-F10 | anchor: A03
Tailgating causes four in ten rear-end crashes, so drivers bank stopping room, brake early and soft, keep the two-second cushion by thousand-counts behind fixed markers with three or four seconds near trucks or weather, shed tailgaters through lane moves or signaled pull-offs without brake jabs, and save side escape room. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=47]

FACT_ID: sec08-F11 | anchor: A04
Belts save lives and curb crash injury, New York mandates adult belts with belts boosters or seats for children, and primary enforcement lets officers stop solely for bare shoulders, ticketing drivers passengers and visitors for the lapse. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=48]

FACT_ID: sec08-F12 | anchor: A04
Unbelted drivers pay fifty dollars, unbelted sixteen-plus riders pay fifty dollars one belt apiece, and drivers answer twenty-five to one hundred dollars plus three points per unrestrained under-sixteen occupant. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=48]

FACT_ID: sec08-F13 | anchor: A04
Under-fours ride approved seats on belts or universal anchors rear-facing to age two or maker limits with convertibles outlasting infant carriers, while four-to-sevens take approved boosters on lap-shoulder belts per maker sizing since car belts alone never qualify. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=48]

FACT_ID: sec08-F14 | anchor: A04
Eight-to-fifteens belt singly with restraints urged under four-nine or one hundred pounds and belts freed past those marks from age four given true fit, exemptions spare emergency rigs pre-sixty-five iron most buses working rural carriers young for-hire riders and certified conditions, and all stay tied since loose bodies fly. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=48]

FACT_ID: sec08-F15 | anchor: A05
Drivers set headrests lock doors and trunk heavy cargo, pair bags with belts for head-on cushions control and fewer second hits, sit ten inches chest-to-cover with hands at three and nine, and never front-seat a rear-facing infant before a live passenger bag. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=49]

FACT_ID: sec08-F16 | anchor: A05
Work zones double speeding fines even crewless amid abrupt slowdowns shifted lanes and close workers, orange diamonds and sign-equal flaggers command slow alert obedience, and smart drivers detour, merge early, honor distance boards, gap two-plus seconds against chronic rear-enders, clear barriers and rigs, and trail mobile zones to the end sign. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=49]

FACT_ID: sec08-F17 | anchor: A06
Roundabouts swing traffic counterclockwise round central islands under yield entry, stand on gap-waiting low curved-approach speeds with deflection decisive, and hold every circling vehicle to thirty miles per hour. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=50]

FACT_ID: sec08-F18 | anchor: A06
Approachers heed lane signs slow for crosswalk walkers peer left at prioritized circlers slip through true gaps leave crosswalks open behind queues share lanes with circulating cyclists and never overtake bikes inside. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=50]

FACT_ID: sec08-F19 | anchor: A07
Circlers ride counterclockwise with fresh priority signal right outward and yield exit crosswalks, walkers keep paths and marked crossings off central islands crossing lane by lane through splitter refuges with eyes open despite priority, and riders either circulate vehicularly at circle pace with right-hand exit signals or dismount to cross on foot. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=51]

FACT_ID: sec08-F20 | anchor: A07
Fatigue retards reactions dulls awareness and warps judgment toward crashes like drink and drugs, betrays itself in closing eyes nodding heads yawns stray thoughts lost miles drift tailgating missed signs lane jerks and rumble hits, and preys on the sleepless unbroken long-haulers night owls medicated drinkers loners dull-road drivers road warriors youths shift hands and sleep-disordered sufferers needing doctors. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=51]

FACT_ID: sec08-F21 | anchor: A08
Prevention banks sleep recruits companions pauses each one hundred miles or two hours rejects alcohol and dulling drugs per pharmacist counsel and grounds the ill exhausted or minutes-awake, while the fading driver concedes unpredictable sleep shuns radio-window ruses parks safe at first signs naps fifteen to forty-five minutes off-road and grants caffeine thirty minutes to bite. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=52]

FACT_ID: sec08-F22 | anchor: A08
Handheld calls cost first-timers two hundred dollars and five points with touches only to open or close and exemptions for emergencies and uniformed crews beside always-legal hands-free, while thumb-typing draws two hundred first, two fifty within eighteen months second, four fifty within eighteen months after, plus junior and probationary bans of one hundred twenty days then a year-plus within six months of return. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=52]

FACT_ID: sec08-F23 | anchor: A09
No vehicle works public roads sans yearly inspection yet makers guide upkeep and wrenches fix faults now, owners babysit brakes steering lights tires and horns, and operators own roadworthiness absolutely. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=53]

FACT_ID: sec08-F24 | anchor: A09
Pulling brakes want drying light-pedal runs then shop care with instant attention to fading feel, steering tolerates scant free play watched booster fluid and quick whine checks, and lamps stay clean whole and aimed for best night sight. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=53]

FACT_ID: sec08-F25 | anchor: A09
Tires hold two thirty-seconds tread read by wear bars and Lincoln-penny probes while cord cuts bulges and bumps ground the car with maker pressures gauge-checked, glass clears via wipers defrosters and fluid, horns warn rather than vent and heal fast. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=53]

FACT_ID: sec08-F26 | anchor: A09
The chapter closes quizzing straight-ahead scanning, unposted city speed, limit safety, minimum purpose, belt duty, trip fatigue, rage meaning and dodging, and safe zone and circle driving. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=53]
